explanations.10: The first number (11444) is the port on your computer; the second number (11434) is the port inside the container—Docker forwards traffic from your 11444 to the container's 11434.
explanations.12: This creates a named storage volume called 'ollama_data' that persists data even if the container stops, and mounts it to the /root/.ollama folder inside the container.
explanations.28: The dot (.) means 'current directory on my computer', and the colon separates it from /workspaces/blog_analyzer, which is the matching folder path inside the container.
explanations.32: This command keeps the container alive indefinitely instead of exiting immediately after startup, so you can actually use it.
